issues.body: `aggregate()` computes `other_pct` from the entire OTHER bucket. That bucket contains both `rule == "unmatched"` steps and intentionally recognized `script-gate` steps such as guards, ratchets, reports, and scoreboards. `render_markdown()` then labels this value "Unclassified share", and `--max-other-pct` uses it as the classifier-decay threshold. Consequently, a workflow whose every step is successfully classified can report a large unclassified share or fail the threshold merely because it spends time in recognized guard/report work. This contradicts the script and research record's claim that the metric detects rules that no longer match real step names.
issues.fix_hint: Track unmatched duration separately during decomposition/aggregation (for example, sum only the `unmatched` rule duration), compute and threshold `unclassified_pct` from that value, and keep the full OTHER bucket as a separate workload category. Add a test containing a long recognized `script-gate` step and assert that OTHER grows while the unclassified percentage remains zero; retain a separate unmatched-step test that makes the threshold fail. Update labels/docs to distinguish OTHER workload from unmatched classification time.
issues.title: Unclassified-share metric includes deliberately classified OTHER steps

verdict.summary: The instrument is well structured and its hermetic tests cover many important seams, but the primary classifier-health metric is not what the CLI and design record claim it is. `other_pct` includes intentionally classified guard/report/ratchet time as well as genuinely unmatched time, yet it is rendered and thresholded as the "unclassified share". This can falsely diagnose classifier decay and make `--max-other-pct` fail even when every step is recognized, undermining the steering data's stated interpretation. The tests currently reinforce the conflation rather than exercising a recognized-OTHER control.
